chapter: With Benny Goodman and Louis Armstrong
title: George Washington, the trombonist
summary: Portrait of trombonist George Washington and his affair with Israel Crosby.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: had another knick knack in the band -- George Washington, trombone player. He was sort of on the byside. He was 21 before he even knew whether he wanted to be a man or a woman. And he accidentally married a woman. And he had a son, but as years went by, he felt this other thing coming out stronger. So he had a love affair with Israel Crosby, the late Israel Crosby. And they would lay on the back seat of the busses, from town to town. But invariably, once a month, we would have to leave George Washington, just like a woman. We'd have to leave him wherever we was. Now, he would see boys out in the audience. He'd get them backstage somehow, buy them clothes. Next day, he's got a woman with him. He was just funny. Everyone was trying to put him on me, (laughs) I say, "You want him to get hurt?" We had a good time, though. He'd tell me and Sid all of his inner secrets, you know. What he would do and what he wouldn't do, how did other people react to him and everything. We'd sit and just laugh.
